Chapter 10: Practicing, Reflecting, and Growing as a Speaker
You know, becoming a truly effective speaker isn’t something that just happens overnight. It’s a journey—one that keeps unfolding, the more you put yourself out there and learn from every experience.
I like to think of each speaking opportunity as its own stepping stone. Some speeches might feel effortless, while others can really test your nerves. But here's the thing—every single one gives you a chance to grow.
So, how do you keep improving? There are a few habits that really make a difference:
First, ask for honest feedback from people you trust. What did they enjoy about your talk? What could you do better next time? Sometimes, an outside perspective shows us things we’d never notice on our own.
After you speak, take a few moments to reflect. Jot down what felt strong, and what you want to improve. This quick review helps those lessons stick.
Recording yourself is another powerful tool. Watching or listening back—even if it feels awkward at first—lets you spot habits and new opportunities to grow.
Try setting small, specific goals. Maybe you’ll focus on making better eye contact, or play with the pace of your delivery. Tackling one thing at a time keeps it manageable and rewarding.
And don’t forget to celebrate your progress—even the tiniest wins. Every bit of improvement matters, and encouragement fuels growth.
Over time, these simple practices don’t just make you a better speaker—they help you build self-awareness and resilience. The more you speak, the more natural it feels, and the more you'll uncover your own unique voice.
So keep stepping up, keep reflecting, and let yourself grow with every opportunity.
